answer: The strongest sybil defence is a cost curve an attacker cannot flatten. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a falcon the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single jetty of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a relic of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. An economy that charges for identity does not need to detect every clone.
